tex_content.html:
egin{exercise} \end{exercise} 1. ch7:7-12Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and let $ abla $ be any connection on $TM$. We can define the curvature endomorphism of $ abla $ by the same formula as in the Riemannian case: $R(X,Y)Z = abla _X abla _Y Z - abla _Y abla _X Z - abla _{[X,Y]}Z$. Then $ abla $ is said to be a flat connection if $R(X,Y)Z \equiv 0$. Prove that the following are equivalent:

  1. $ abla $ is flat.

  2. For every point $p \in M$, there exists a parallel local frame defined on a neighborhood of $p$.

  3. For all $p,q \in M$, parallel transport along an admissible curve segment $\gamma $ from $p$ to $q$ depends only on the path-homotopy class of $\gamma $.

  4. Parallel transport around any sufficiently small closed curve is the identity; that is, for every $p \in M$, there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $p$ such that if $\gamma : [a,b] o U$ is an admissible curve in $U$ starting and ending at $p$, then $P_{ab} : T_p M o T_p M$ is the identity map.

\end{exercise}
